parsed.draft_response:
Hi — thanks for the details. I’m sorry this is impacting your client launch.

Based on what you shared, the project was deleted and then restored within the retention window, but some files and comments are still missing. That typically means we’ll need to review the restore outcome (and related logs) to confirm what was actually brought back and why some items didn’t reappear.

To help our engineering team investigate quickly, could you reply with the following:
1) Which workspace/project is affected (project name + any ID you have)? Also confirm which product/module this is in (e.g., which platform).
2) Exact timestamps for: deletion and the restore click (and your time zone).
3) After the restore, are the missing items entirely gone or partially present? If possible, list 3–10 specific files/comments that are missing.
4) Did the restore action show any success message, errors, or warnings? If available, include the restore job/operation ID.
5) Any relevant logs/screenshots from the restore attempt (including any “restore completed”/“failed” indicators).
6) Confirm whether the same user/team member accounts are accessing the restored project now (in case access/permissions changed).

We’ve marked this for human review/escalation on our engineering side due to the critical business impact. Once we have the items above, we’ll take a closer look at the restore records and the state of the project content after restore.
promised_actions: Review the restore records and the restored project state once the requested details are provided.
safety_notes: Do not claim recovery is possible or guarantee an outcome.
Do not promise a refund or specific SLA.
Request minimal but sufficient information to investigate missing items after restore.

The team clicked restore within the retention window.
After restore, several files and comments are still missing.
The project contains the final deliverables for a client launch on Monday.
